messages:
ana: noticed a spike in org-attributed requests in the quota dashboard. the requests came from keys that should be project-scoped but console shows "org" only.
trent: do you have an example request id? might be a proxy routing case where X-Project header was dropped.
nana: typo: it's me (ana). sample curl below from the customer trace: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_org_zzz' \ 
  -H 'X-User-Consent: consent=consent-9' \ 
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
trent: thanks. so the token is an org key and consent present. expected: exchange fills project claim if user consent linked to a project. observed: no project claim in auth metadata, so quota aggregator collapses to org bucket.
nora: we have three options: 1) exchange synthesizes a project id and returns it in the auth response/body 2) exchange sets a response header (X-Assigned-Project) that downstream reads 3) keep current behavior and teach quota pipeline to look up consent->project mappings.
lee: my vote is #2 (header). minimal changes, explicit, and downstreams can opt-in. avoids creating fake projects in storage.
nana: downside: requires every downstream service to opt-in (console, billing, telemetry, quota-agg). that's significant churn.
trent: #1 centralizes behavior and hides complexity, but we must add clear telemetry to mark synthetic so billing doesn't treat it as a "real" project. also need an org-level opt-out so customers who don't want synthetic projects keep old attribution.
nora: metrics we'd emit if #1: auth.exchange.assigned_project.count, tags: {synthetic:true|false, org_id:<org>}. add auth.exchange.assigned_project.latency too.
lee: for headers we'd emit auth.exchange.assigned_project.header_emitted=true and include header value. still need billing mapping change either way.
nana: operational ask: whichever approach, add original_token_type to auth logs (org_key|project_key|sa_key) and consent_id so support can trace.
trent: agree. also add a flag auth.synthetic_project_mode with values: header|synthetic|none so we can flip per-org via feature flags.
nora: console UX: show a subtle pill "(org default)" next to assigned project name and a tooltip "Assigned because org-level consent — not a user-created project". hide from project picker unless user clicks "show org defaults".
nana: billing: ensure invoice generator ignores synthetic projects unless the org explicitly maps them. add migration script to collapse historical synthetic metrics into org bucket for existing customers.
lee: tests: unit for exchange behavior + integration test where quota-agg receives either header or project claim and verifies per-project quota decrement. add telemetry test asserting synthetic=true tag when applicable.
trent: I'll draft RFC with sequence diagrams and a rollout plan: start with header=false default, canary on 1 org with header=true then move to synthetic with explicit billing mapping.
nora: one more subtlety: fallback when consent references multiple projects. exchange should pick the project linked to the consent used for that call, not arbitrarily pick first. include consent_project_id field.
nana: good catch. include consent_project_id in auth metadata and telemetry.
lee: small ops note: if we add synthetic projects to DB, ensure we namespace them as synthetic/org-<id>-<ts> and TTL them if org later creates a real project with same name.
trent: PR incoming. tagging @deploy-bot to queue a canary run when PR lands.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary, ref=pr/3180, flags: auth.synthetic_project_mode=header
lee: splitting work: i'll own exchange header + telemetry, trent owns RFC + feature flagging, nora handles console UX, nana will coordinate billing migration.
trent: thanks all. will post RFC link and runbook in this thread.
deploy-bot: canary deployed at 1767010020
